stage_probability.definition: P(AI providers, model labs + chip layer, capture >= 50% of the automation surplus for >= 2 consecutive years at some point 2027-2045 | S1 and S2 with onset ~Triangular(2028,2032,2040)). Automation surplus = displaced labour cost (at the S2-depressed wage) minus true compute resource cost.
stage_probability.ci_method: STRUCTURAL band: min-max of calibrated P across 64 model variants (conduct mapping x kappa spec x pricing spec x period length x copula). Central = equal-weight mean of variants. Not a statistical CI.

timeline.definition: base spec: second year of first 2-year window with K>=0.5, among draws where S3 occurs by 2045 (calibration-weighted); censored at 2045

notes_for_integrator: Use stage_probability.mean (structural central) with ci_low/ci_high as a structural range, not a CI.
Price and rent are now consistent: rent <= spend <= wage in every draw-year; calibrated to 2027 lab gross margin ~0.5 and spend ~0.1 of displaced wage.
The biggest structural swing is pricing: static equilibrium vs penetration pricing (low now, raise later) which is the scenario text's own mechanism.
S3 events concentrate in worlds where open-weight releases stop or collusion forms; S3 therefore anti-correlates with Alternative B (decentralised AI) viability.
Enforcement is weakened by rentier capture that rises with demand collapse: link to S4.
Post-2035 events are lower-confidence extrapolation (see derived.share_of_events_after_2035).

priors.z_speed: N(0,1) shared capability-speed latent; Gaussian copula rho=0.5 (base) with T2 (earlier), D_max (higher), N_inf (lower), g_tau (more negative), L_inf (longer).
priors.hhi_2026: Triangular(2200, 2800, 3500). Menlo Ventures 2025 enterprise LLM API share (Anthropic ~40, OpenAI ~27, Google ~21).
priors.N_inf: Lognormal median 4.0 (HHI 2500), 90% 2.3-7: long-run effective number of frontier suppliers (entry from China, Meta, xAI, sovereign labs vs 2.4x/yr training cost growth, Cottier et al. 2024).
priors.k_N: Uniform(0.1, 0.3)/yr: OU reversion speed of log N_eff.
priors.beta_exit: Uniform(0, 0.6): reduction of log N_inf per unit demand collapse D (revenue base shrinks under S2).
priors.lag0: Lognormal median 4 months, 90% 3-7 (Epoch AI open-closed ECI gap).
priors.L_inf: Lognormal median 6, 90% 3-12 months: long-run open-weight lag while releases continue (research: 2030 median 6; observed flat 3-4 months 2023-2026).
priors.k_L: Uniform(0.15, 0.5)/yr: OU reversion speed of log lag.
priors.h_close: Beta(mean 0.03, sd 0.02)/yr: hazard that ALL major open releasers stop near-frontier releases (needs US labs and Chinese labs, for whom open release is a geopolitical strategy).
priors.h_reopen: Uniform(0.05, 0.3)/yr: reopening hazard (other jurisdiction, new entrant, DeepSeek-type shock).
priors.tau0: Lognormal median 10 months, 90% 4-30: e-folding time scale of economic value of recent capability progress.
priors.g_tau: Normal(0, 0.07)/yr drift of log tau: symmetric between acceleration (frontier months worth more) and saturation (commodity models do professional work).
priors.a_cond: Uniform(0.5, 1.0): theta = N_eff^-a (a=1 homogeneous Cournot; lower = differentiation softens competition). theta=1 at monopoly.
priors.delta_annual: Beta(mean 0.85, sd 0.06): providers' annual discount factor; per-period delta = delta^(1/periods), periods=4 (quarterly price adjustment) in base.
priors.n_out: Uniform(1, 4): additional effective players in the collusion game outside N_eff (Chinese frontier labs, open fringe); halved while open releases are stopped.
priors.h_coll0: Uniform(0.02, 0.2)/yr: hazard of entering a tacit-collusion regime at N_coll=2 when feasible; scaled exp(-0.3 (N_coll-2)) and by early tech turbulence (judgement; no documented tacit collusion in fast-moving software markets).
priors.tech_uncert: Uniform(0.3, 0.8): early tech-turbulence reduction of collusion entry hazard, decays with 8y time constant.
priors.p_break: Uniform(0.05, 0.25)/yr: exogenous breakdown of a collusive regime (new entrant, capability leap, defection).
priors.war_frac: Uniform(0.1, 0.4): Green-Porter fraction of time in price wars within a collusive regime.
priors.theta_coll: Uniform(0.5, 1.0): conduct within the collusive regime (mapped through S(theta)).
priors.kappa_curv: spec 'curvature' (base): task-value demand q=(1-x)^s, s~Lognormal(1, 0.3-3) gives single-price monopoly share of realised surplus (1+s)/(1+2s); plus price discrimination disc~U(0,0.5) of the remainder; minus buyer power bp~U(0,0.3). Limit price bounded by wage.
priors.kappa_barg: spec 'bargaining': Beta(mean 0.4, sd 0.12): Nash bargaining with large enterprise buyers who can threaten to self-supply.
priors.kappa_limit: spec 'limit' (high end): Beta(mean 0.85, sd 0.07): provider limit-prices just below the (falling) wage with near-perfect discrimination via per-seat / per-outcome enterprise contracts; the only outside option is human labour.
priors.eps_D: Uniform(0, 0.3): reduction of kappa per unit D (customer-viability constraint: squeezing failing customers kills demand).
priors.omega_w: Uniform(0.2, 0.8): wage fall per unit D (displaced workers bid wages down, lowering the price cap).
priors.sw0: Lognormal median 0.10, 90% 0.02-0.4: switching cost as fraction of spend (Dataiku: 55% switched; 81% use 3+ families).
priors.lambda_sq: Uniform(1.5, 2.5): loss-aversion / status-quo multiplier on switching cost.
priors.g_lock: Uniform(0.0, 0.15)/yr: growth of lock-in from agentic memory, workflows, proprietary data.
priors.reg0: Uniform(0, 0.25): baseline behavioural regulation cut to lock-in from 2027 (EU Data Act egress ban, DMA; EU ~20% of market).
priors.sigma_max: Uniform(0.0, 0.3): max share of frontier-task demand that buyers self-supply (large enterprises distilling from frontier outputs or training own models; hyperscalers already counted in N_eff). Frontier-only tasks by definition exceed open capability, so self-supply is limited.
priors.rho_self: Uniform(0.2, 0.6): frontier Lerner index at which self-supply reaches 63% of its max.
priors.q0: Lognormal median 0.05, 90% 0.015-0.17: market compute cost per automated task in 2027 as fraction of wage (judgement; calibrated jointly with markup to spend/margin observables).
priors.c_decl: Uniform(0.7, 1.0)/yr: decline of compute cost per task (40x/yr at fixed capability offset by agentic token growth and frontier-tier pricing; research frontier-tier price trend -15%/yr, -60% to +50%).
priors.chip_share: Uniform(0.35, 0.6): chip share of compute cost.
priors.chip_margin_2032: Uniform(0.4, 0.75): accelerator margin after custom-ASIC ramp.
priors.phi0: penetration spec only: Uniform(0.1, 1.0) ratio of 2027 markup to equilibrium markup; converges at k_phi~U(0.05, 0.3)/yr.
priors.vis_thresh: Uniform(0.25, 0.4): capture share at which rent becomes salient.
priors.h_file0: Beta(mean 0.15, sd 0.07)/yr: base hazard of suit / ex-ante rule once salient.
priors.eta_rentier: Uniform(0, 0.8): extra capture per unit D as the state's tax base shifts to AI firms (S4 rentier logic).
priors.gamma_sal: Uniform(0, 2): salience boost of enforcement per unit D.
priors.p_struct: Beta(mean 0.1, sd 0.06): P(structural remedy | remedy) (AT&T yes; Microsoft, Google no).
priors.b_behav: Uniform(0.2, 0.6): behavioural remedy cut to lock-in and collusion entry.
priors.T2: Triangular(2028, 2032, 2040): S2 demand-collapse onset (conditioning; copula-linked to z).
priors.D_max: Beta(mean 0.35, sd 0.12): peak fraction of aggregate demand lost under S2 (copula-linked to z).
priors.D_width: Uniform(1.5, 4) years: logistic width of cascade (B2C first, B2B lag).
priors.calibration: Importance weights: gross margin 2027 ~ N(0.5, 0.08); spend p_2027 ~ lognormal(median 0.10, sd ln(3)/1.645).
